sections.heading: C2 — Warning signs
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Warning signs

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A04
A DEER CROSSING sign marks an area with frequent deer crossings and a history of deer crashes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A04
Do not enter beneath a LOW CLEARANCE warning if the vehicle's height exceeds the displayed clearance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A04
Shoulder warnings identify pavement edges with a lower shoulder or an unpaved soft shoulder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A04
A LOW SHOULDER warning can identify a shoulder as much as three inches below road level. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A04
SHOULDER DROP OFF warns of a more severe drop than a LOW SHOULDER sign. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A04
If a wheel leaves the pavement onto a low or soft shoulder, do not brake hard or make a sharp steering correction back toward the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A04
A HILL or DOWNGRADE warning calls for slowing and preparing to select a lower gear to control speed and reduce brake wear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A04
TRAFFIC SIGNAL AHEAD warns of a signal that may be hidden by a curve or hill, so reduce speed and be ready to stop if necessary. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A04
A queue may remain ahead when the hidden traffic signal is red or has just turned green. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A04
STOP SIGN AHEAD warns of a potentially hidden stop and queued vehicles, requiring slowing in preparation to stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A04
BICYCLE CROSSING AHEAD warns that riders may cross the vehicle's path and that reducing speed may be necessary. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A04
A bicycle-crossing warning may use a yellow or fluorescent yellow-green background. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A04
At a RAILROAD CROSSING AHEAD warning, begin watching and listening for trains with enough distance left to stop before the tracks if needed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A05
An advance intersection and railroad warning means the side road has tracks shortly beyond the intersection. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A05
Where a side road crosses railroad tracks just beyond an intersection, a driver turning onto that road must be ready to stop if a train approaches. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A05
A bicycle and motor-vehicle SHARE THE ROAD sign at a narrow point warns motorists to leave adequate room for bicycles. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A05
A PEDESTRIAN CROSSING warning at a marked crosswalk or in advance calls for readiness to slow or stop if necessary. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A05
Pedestrian-crossing warnings may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A05
The pentagonal SCHOOL sign warns that a school zone is near. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A05
A downward arrow accompanying a SCHOOL sign locates the school crosswalk at that sign. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A05
At a school warning, reduce speed, watch for children crossing and stop if needed. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A05
A school warning may have a yellow or fluorescent yellow-green background. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A05
HORSE-DRAWN VEHICLE warnings identify areas where slow horse-drawn traffic crosses or shares the roadway. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A05
Roadside hazard markers may warn of structures near the road or dangerous edge conditions such as a drop-off. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A05
The downward angle of a roadside marker's stripes points toward the direction to move to avoid the hazard. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A05
Pass a marked hazard on the right edge to its left, and pass a marked hazard on the left edge to its right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A05
A marker for a center hazard permits passing it on either the left or right. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R28 | anchor: A06
Work-zone warnings are normally orange diamonds with black lettering rather than yellow warning signs. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R29 | anchor: A06
Work-zone signs mark maintenance, construction or utility areas that may contain workers or equipment near the road, so stay alert and reduce speed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R30 | anchor: A06
Headlights must be on through every posted work zone at any time of day, including when work is inactive. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R31 | anchor: A06
A driver stopped by police for a work-zone traffic violation incurs an additional 25-dollar fine if the vehicle's headlights are off. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R32 | anchor: A06
An active work zone has construction, maintenance or utility workers on the road or the shoulder beside an open travel lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R33 | anchor: A06
Active-work-zone boundary signs mark the beginning and end of that active area. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R34 | anchor: A06
ROAD WORK AHEAD announces approaching road work and calls for slowing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R35 | anchor: A06
A LANE CLOSED AHEAD sign identifies the lane closure and its distance ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R36 | anchor: A06
A sign reading RIGHT LANE CLOSED 1000 FT announces closure of the right lane one thousand feet ahead. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R37 | anchor: A06
FLAGGER AHEAD warns of a traffic controller using STOP or SLOW paddles or a red flag to direct traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R38 | anchor: A06
Pay particular attention to flaggers when approaching and passing through a work zone. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R39 | anchor: A06
A WORKERS AHEAD warning requires special care because workers may be on or close to the road. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R40 | anchor: A06
Highway workers can report speeding or unsafe work-zone driving to police, who may issue tickets carrying fines and points. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-R41 | anchor: A06
ROAD CLOSED FLOODING means the road ahead is closed by flooding and the driver must take another route. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0022]
